name: Swallow Falls
blurb: Muddy Creek Falls is the tallest free-falling waterfall in Maryland at 53 feet, and the mile-long loop past it runs through a stand of old-growth hemlock and white pine — some of it over 300 years old, the last of its kind in the state. It is the most visited park in Garrett County and the reason the reservation system exists.

reservation.window: Memorial Day weekend 2026 (23 May) – Labor Day 2026
reservation.days: Weekends and holidays only. Weekdays are entry on arrival.
reservation.bookAhead: Opens 7 days before the visit; changes or cancellations until 8am the day before
reservation.note: Slots are expected to sell out consistently through the summer, so a weekend visit needs planning. On weekdays you can still turn up and pay on arrival.

fee.note: Regular day-use fees are paid when you book. Each reservation also carries a non-refundable service charge of about $1.50 per person. The day-use fee itself is not confirmed.

warnings: Pets are not permitted in the day-use area, including the Canyon Trail, from 23 May to 7 September 2026.
You cannot turn up without a reservation in summer. This is a three-hour drive from Baltimore or DC and the booking window only opens seven days out.

name: Deep Creek Lake
blurb: The state park sits on the northeast shore of Maryland's largest lake, with the only public swimming beach on Deep Creek and a discovery centre that stays open year-round. Everything else on the lake is private shoreline, which is why this one gets busy.

name: Herrington Manor
blurb: A 53-acre lake made by damming Herrington Creek, with twenty year-round cabins built by the Civilian Conservation Corps. No gas motors on the lake, which keeps it quiet. Cross-country ski rental in winter — one of very few places in Maryland where that is a real option.

name: New Germany
blurb: A 13-acre lake on the site of a nineteenth-century milling settlement, wrapped inside Savage River State Forest. Eleven cabins, a groomed cross-country ski network in winter, and enough elevation that it holds snow when the rest of Maryland has none.

name: Big Run
blurb: Three hundred acres at the mouth of the Savage River where it meets the reservoir, surrounded on all sides by Savage River State Forest. Primitive camping, and the put-in for some of the most serious whitewater in the mid-Atlantic when the river is released.

reservation.note: Not on Maryland DNR's list of parks requiring day-use reservations as of 25 June 2026. Day-use fees may still apply on arrival.

fee.note: To be confirmed — small primitive parks are sometimes free.

warnings: Whitewater here depends on scheduled dam releases from the Savage River Reservoir. Without a release there may be no runnable water at all.

name: Casselman River Bridge
blurb: Four acres around an 80-foot stone arch built in 1813 for the National Road — the largest single-span stone arch in America when it was finished, and a National Historic Landmark. A ten-minute stop rather than a day out, and worth it.

name: Sang Run
blurb: A restored 1800s homestead and former general store on the Youghiogheny, kept as a picture of rural life before the lake existed. Also the put-in for the upper Yough, which is genuinely expert-only water.

reservation.note: Not on Maryland DNR's list of parks requiring day-use reservations as of 25 June 2026. Day-use fees may still apply on arrival.

warnings: The upper Youghiogheny below here is expert whitewater and depends on scheduled releases. It is not a place to improvise.

name: Wolf Den Run
blurb: Maryland's designated off-highway vehicle park, on reclaimed mine land above the Potomac's north branch. Miles of ATV and dirt bike trail, plus hiking, fishing and hunting. Unlike anywhere else in the state park system.

name: Youghiogheny Wild River
blurb: Maryland's only designated wild river, running north through a gorge toward Pennsylvania. Managed for the river itself rather than for visitors — few facilities, and the whitewater through here is among the hardest in the east.

reservation.note: Not on Maryland DNR's list of parks requiring day-use reservations as of 25 June 2026. Day-use fees may still apply on arrival.

warnings: Expert whitewater with limited access and limited rescue. Release-dependent.

name: Savage River State Forest
blurb: Maryland's largest state forest at around 54,000 acres, wrapping Big Run and New Germany. Dispersed camping, hunting, trout water and the reservoir behind it. A forest rather than a park — different rules, and worth knowing which you are standing in.

reservation.note: State forests run different rules from state parks. Dispersed camping usually needs a permit. Unconfirmed.

warnings: Hunting is permitted in season across the forest. Check dates and wear blaze orange.
